experiment: M3.1 SOC-domain prompt-injection benchmark v1.0 generation

bcontrol_sampling.method: Reservoir-sampled up to pool_size unique-incident BenignPositive rows while streaming datasets/GUIDE_train.csv once (chunksize=100_000), scored each with the deployed baseline_model.joblib's predict_proba, ranked by Shannon entropy over the 3-class distribution, kept the top 100. This ranks within a large random subsample of the full BenignPositive population, not the full multi-million-row column -- stated plainly rather than implying an exhaustive scan.

caveat: The 400 attack rows are template-generated synthetic payloads, authored for this benchmark rather than drawn from real attacker traffic -- the same methodology already disclosed for the smaller 40-row corpus this replaces (Section 6.2). The 100 BCONTROL rows are real GUIDE BenignPositive alerts. Interrater agreement on a 100-row blinded subset is tracked separately (see m3_1_interrater_kappa.py) and is not yet available -- it requires two independent human raters, not generated here.
